issues.should_be: Possible exclusion under Article 3.1 (driver had alcohol above the legal limit / under the influence) — the claim must be referred to a Veridia claims handler per Article 3 ('An exclusion is never applied automatically. When a claim shows a possible exclusion, it is referred to a claims handler, who decides') and Article 7.2, and must not be paid automatically
issues.evidence: Customer email dated 2026-10-22: 'Coming back from a friend's birthday party, where I had a few drinks, I lost control and hit a fence.' Veridia contract (document 2630#10414, contract.pdf): Article 3.1 exclusion list on page 2, referral rule at end of Article 3 on page 2, and Article 7.2 on page 3

verdict.summary: All recorded facts (policy VER-1004, C2 coverage in the Policy Schedule, incident 2026-10-21 reported 2026-10-22 within the 5-day deadline of Article 4.1, €1,800 repair cost, at fault, no third party, photos and repair quote provided, €300 deductible with no young-driver surcharge since the licence dates from 2008, assessor required since €1,800 > €1,500) match the email and contract, but the email states the driver had 'a few drinks' before losing control, which is a possible alcohol exclusion under Article 3.1 that the handler recorded as null — per Articles 3 and 7.2 this claim must be referred to a claims handler and must not be paid automatically, so do not approve the staged payment yet.
